name: Depth Ripple Geometry Setup
instruction: Populate res://scenes/main.tscn so Main contains a water depth visualization scene: add a WorldEnvironment with a procedural sky and glow enabled, a DirectionalLight3D with shadows enabled, a MeshInstance3D named Water that uses a 10x10 PlaneMesh subdivided 20x20 with a ShaderMaterial pointing at res://scenes/WaterShader.tres, a Background Node3D holding exactly 5 sphere MeshInstance3Ds at these positions (all within the 10x10 water plane): Sphere at (1.500, 0.200, -4.200); Sphere2 at (-1.000, -0.500, -3.800); Sphere3 at (2.800, 0.000, -4.500); Sphere4 at (-2.600, -0.400, -3.300); Sphere5 at (0.000, 0.400, -4.000), all with green StandardMaterial3D overrides, and a Camera3D positioned at (0.007, 0.600, -0.200) with a FOV of 110 and all spheres are visible.

metadata.tutorial_source: YouTube: Bramwell - Tutorial: Improving 3D Water in Godot 4
metadata.transcript_excerpt: add a mesh instance 3D set the mesh to whatever shape you want to see how it intersects let's try a sphere and then you can fiddle with its scale and position

key_properties.Background spheres: Green StandardMaterial3D overrides at the instructed positions (5 spheres)
